$comment: $defs library (like geo and subdivision-code): reference a scalar by fragment, e.g. https://resources.rusl.com/resources/pragmatic/schemas/contact.scalars#/$defs/email.

email.description: An email address, validated deliberately lightly: format: email plus the RFC-derived length cap -- no pattern. In draft 2020-12, format is annotation-only unless a validator opts into the format-assertion vocabulary, and that is the intended posture here: syntax policing beyond this is theater -- the only validation that actually proves an address is reachable is sending a confirmation message to it, which no schema can perform. maxLength 254 is the practical address-length cap derived from RFC 5321's 256-octet forward-path limit minus the two angle brackets that wrap the path on the wire, not a stylistic choice.
email.title: Email address

phone.description: E.164 international phone number in storage form: a leading "+" followed by 1-15 digits (country calling code plus subscriber number) -- no spaces, dashes, parentheses, or leading zero. This is the STORAGE format, not a display format -- national/local formats (e.g. "(415) 555-0100") must be normalized to E.164 before persisting (libphonenumber or equivalent handles the country-specific rules this schema deliberately does not encode). Extensions are NOT part of E.164 and are NOT captured here -- callers needing an extension add a separate extension field on the containing schema rather than appending it to this value. Rendering a stored number for display (national grouping, dashes, parentheses) is a presentation concern for the UI layer, not this schema.
phone.title: E.164 phone number

description: Scalar value types for the contact package, published as a $defs library and referenced by fragment. Holds the shapes too small to earn standalone schemas: email and phone.
title: Contact scalar types
